messages:
olivia: Quick Q on /v1/rerank: when we return items, do we guarantee deterministic ordering when scores tie? Some clients rely on stable output. Also: what are the score semantics (bounded, relative)? Any backward-compat for clients expecting an integer `rank` field?

sam: For the current spec we added `scores: [float]` and `items: [{id, score, ...}]`. We need a concrete tie-breaker. I vote for deterministic fallback to `input_index` to preserve original order (stable sort).

miguel: `input_index` is fine if callers keep order, but a lot of pipelines re-batch. Recommend fallback to `original_id` when present, then `input_index`. Also clarify: scores are relative floats, unbounded — higher is better. We'll explicitly document "higher score wins".

karen: From PM/customer side: legacy clients expect `rank` ints. Can we keep `rank` (1-based position) in response to avoid breaking? Also include a short migration note.

sam: Adding `rank` is backward compatible. We should codify `tie_policy` in the API: allowed values `stable_input_index` (default), `lexicographic_id`, or `deterministic_hash`. Avoid `random`.

tina: Strong - no `random`. Also prefer avoiding automatic normalization. If someone wants normalized scores, they can pass `normalize=true` and we return `score_normalized: true` for each item.

olivia: Example request/response for docs:

```
POST /v1/rerank
{
  "model": "rwd/rerank-2b",
  "items": [
    {"id": "docA", "text": "..."},
    {"id": "docB", "text": "..."}
  ],
  "tie_policy": "stable_input_index"
}

200 OK
{
  "items": [
    {"id": "docB", "score": 0.732, "rank": 1},
    {"id": "docA", "score": 0.732, "rank": 2}
  ],
  "note": "scores are relative floats; identical scores ordered per tie_policy"
}
```

miguel: Tests: add unit that constructs identical scores and assert ordering stable for `stable_input_index` and lexicographic for `lexicographic_id`. I'll add to rerank-core tests.

deploy-bot: CI ✅ spec-pr/452

olivia: I'll open the docs PR to add `tie_policy` + migration note. Will include above example and a small FAQ. Thanks :thumbsup:
